closing_stairs.description: The curse is not the weight of the world, but the atrophy of the foundational pillars. If a territory harmoniously develops its three shoulders —the ecological basin (E), the caring community (S), and regenerative capital (K)— the rock stops rolling down toward the abyss and becomes a celestial sphere ascending steadily up the marble stairs toward sovereignty.

philosophy_modal.title: Philosophy of Shoulders: From Sisyphus to Atlas
philosophy_modal.subtitle: The curse is not the weight of the world, but the atrophy of the foundational pillars.
philosophy_modal.p1_bold: Why does Sisyphus push the boulder while Atlas upholds the world?
philosophy_modal.p1_rest: Traditional economics conceives development as a rolling boulder: accelerated extraction, entropic consumption, and perpetual reconstruction after collapse. That is the curse of Sisyphus.
philosophy_modal.p2: HOMBROS posits that if a territory harmoniously develops its three shoulders —the ecological watershed (E), the caring community (S), and regenerative capital (K)— the boulder stops rolling toward the abyss and transforms into a celestial sphere ascending steadily up the stairway toward sovereignty.
philosophy_modal.shoulder_e_desc: Clean water, living soil health, and watershed photosynthesis.
philosophy_modal.shoulder_s_desc: Neighborhood cohesion, mutual care, and non-violent territorial peace.
philosophy_modal.shoulder_k_desc: Productive autonomy, absence of usury, and regenerative capital.
